title: Moses and the Runaway Young Goat
text:
Before he led Israel out of Egypt, Moses was a shepherd in Midian, tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro. The rabbis tell what happened one day in the wilderness.

A young goat broke away from the flock and ran off. Moses went after it. It ran until it came to a shaded spot where there was a pool of water, and there it stopped and began to drink.

When Moses caught up, he understood. "I did not know you were running because you were thirsty," he said. "You must be tired." He lifted the little animal onto his shoulders and carried it back to the flock.

The midrash says that God then declared: "You have shown such compassion in leading the flock of a mere mortal. By your life, you shall shepherd My flock, Israel." Soon afterward, Moses came upon the burning bush.
lesson: When someone strays or falls behind, find out why before you judge. How you treat the weakest member of a group is the best evidence of whether you can be trusted with the whole.
caveat: The midrash speaks of a young goat (kid), though popular retellings often make it a lamb.
